facts.value: Christianity is based on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth (1st century) as presented in the New Testament.
The Christian faith is essentially faith in Jesus as the Christ, the Son of God, and as Savior and Lord.
Most Christians believe in the Trinity, which teaches the unity of Father, Son (Jesus Christ), and Holy Spirit as three persons in one Godhead.
Most Christians can describe their faith with the Nicene Creed.
Christianity has been propagated throughout the world via missionary work and was the religion of the Byzantine Empire in the first millennium and of Western Europe during the time of colonization.
It is the world's largest religion, with about 2.3 billion followers as of 2015.
The main divisions of Christianity are the Catholic Church, Eastern Christianity, and Protestantism.
The Catholic Church is led by the Bishop of Rome and the bishops worldwide in communion with him.
Eastern Christianity includes Eastern Orthodoxy, Oriental Orthodoxy, and the Church of the East.
Protestantism separated from the Catholic Church in the 16th-century Protestant Reformation and is split into thousands of denominations.
Major branches of Protestantism include Anglicanism, Baptists, Calvinism, Lutheranism, and Methodism.
Smaller groups include Restorationism, the Latter-day Saint movement, and Jehovah's Witnesses.
